hero.headline: Zelensky warns of major Russian attacks within 48 hours
hero.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects Russia to launch major attacks within the next two days based on intelligence from the U.S. and European allies.
hero.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is preparing for a major Russian attack that he expects to occur within the next 48 hours. The warning is based on intelligence shared by the U.S. and European allies.

Zelensky said he believes the attacks will happen either tonight or tomorrow night. He indicated the anticipated assault would be significant in scale based on the intelligence assessments provided by Western partners.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal negotiated by his envoys
cards.teaser: President Trump has asked for several amendments to the deal his envoys reached with Iranian counterparts, according to a senior administration official and a s.
cards.body:
President Trump asked his advisers to make amendments to a framework agreement reached between U.S. and Iranian negotiators, according to administration officials. The president met with his team to make what he described as his "final determination" on the deal during a Friday Situation Room meeting.

The tentative agreement would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Trump's requested changes have initiated another round of negotiations between the parties as both sides work to finalize terms.

cards.headline: Japan defense minister rejects militarism accusations, criticizes China's weapons buildup
cards.teaser: Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi denied charges of militarism while making pointed remarks about China's arsenal in an escalating dispute over Japan's military expansion.
cards.body:
Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi rejected China's accusations of neo-militarism, delivering some of Tokyo's strongest remarks yet in the dispute over military expansion. He characterized Japan as a "peace-loving" nation while criticizing China for expanding its military capabilities "without sufficient transparency."

Under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, Japan has accelerated its shift toward a more proactive defense policy, moving away from its post-World War II pacifist stance with U.S. support. Koizumi pledged to continue strengthening the military despite Beijing's criticism of Tokyo's increasingly assertive security approach, while calling for candid dialogue between the nations.

cards.headline: UN adds Israeli and Russian forces to sexual violence blacklist
cards.teaser: The United Nations placed Israeli and Russian security forces on its annual blacklist documenting sexual violence during conflict for the first time.
cards.body:
The United Nations included Israeli and Russian security forces on its annual blacklist for sexual violence during conflict for the first time in a report released Friday. The U.N. document identifies 77 government and non-government parties credibly suspected of patterns of rape or other sexual violence.

The additions follow allegations of rape against detained Palestinians by Israeli forces. The blacklist tracks parties across multiple countries engaged in ongoing conflicts where sexual violence has been documented.

cards.headline: Taiwan debates security measures after Chinese-born woman accused of infiltration
cards.teaser: A Chinese-born woman's infiltration case has sparked debate in Taiwan over balancing democratic defense with treatment of mainland spouses.
cards.body:
A Chinese-born woman accused of infiltration has triggered debate in Taiwan about how the island defends its democracy while maintaining fair treatment of mainland Chinese migrants. The case has made mainland spouses a focus of infiltration concerns.

Taiwan faces tension between protecting itself from potential security threats and avoiding discrimination against the thousands of people who have moved to the island from China through marriage. The debate centers on developing security measures that do not unfairly target an entire group based on origin.

cards.headline: Ebola outbreak in DR Congo kills over 245, WHO chief visits affected region
cards.body:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has resulted in 65 confirmed deaths, with 246 suspected cases reported in the conflict-affected Ituri province. The region borders Uganda and South Sudan, raising concerns about cross-border transmission.

The World Health Organization chief has arrived in the country to support containment efforts as the outbreak spreads. The WHO estimates the death rate between 30 and 50 percent among confirmed cases. "It's huge. It means that up to five out of 10 people are likely to die," said Anaïs Legand from the WHO's high threat pathogens team.

Uganda's health ministry confirmed its own outbreak, with a 59-year-old man dying in a Kampala hospital after traveling from the DRC. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention expressed concern about further spread, particularly given the movement of people in mining towns within Ituri province where cases have been concentrated.

Medical charity Doctors Without Borders described the situation as deeply alarming. Aid agencies report that local health workers lack adequate equipment to treat patients and prevent transmission of the virus.

Laboratory testing has identified a significant challenge in the response. The DRC's national research laboratory detected Ebola virus in 13 of 20 samples tested, with results showing the Bundibugyo strain. This strain differs from the more common Zaire strain found in previous DRC outbreaks. Critically, no licensed vaccine exists for Bundibugyo, though vaccines are available for the Zaire strain. Only two previous outbreaks of Bundibugyo occurred, in 2007 and 2012.

The Africa CDC announced an urgent meeting scheduled for Friday involving authorities from the DRC, Uganda, and South Sudan, alongside the WHO and pharmaceutical companies. "Given the high population movement between affected areas and neighbouring countries, rapid regional coordination is essential," said Dr. Jean Kaseya, director general of Africa CDC.

Cases have been reported primarily in the Mongwalu and Rwampara health zones, with suspected cases also emerging in neighboring Bunia. The DRC has experienced 16 Ebola outbreaks since the virus was first identified there in 1976.

Experts point to several factors contributing to regular outbreaks in the region. Close human contact with animal reservoirs, likely bats and possibly primates, combined with movement between rural and urban areas, tropical climate, and extensive rainforest coverage create conditions favoring transmission.

Health organizations are deploying additional personnel and supplies to support the response. The speed of outbreak containment will depend on implementing effective measures and providing resources to medical teams caring for patients while preventing new infections. The situation underscores the challenges disease control faces in conflict-affected regions with limited infrastructure and high population mobility.

cards.headline: Israeli soldiers describe ongoing killings in Gaza despite ceasefire
cards.teaser: Israeli soldiers provided rare firsthand accounts from Gaza, telling reporters that killings continue despite an official ceasefire.
cards.body:
Israeli soldiers have provided accounts to the Associated Press describing continued violence in Gaza that contradicts the official ceasefire declaration. One soldier characterized calling the situation a ceasefire as "a joke," citing ongoing killings in the territory.

These firsthand accounts offer a stark contrast to official descriptions of conditions on the ground. The soldiers' testimonies highlight the gap between the ceasefire's announcement and the reality they are witnessing in Gaza.

cards.headline: Hundreds arrested in France after PSG Champions League victory celebrations turn violent
cards.teaser: French authorities arrested more than 280 people as celebrations of PSG's Champions League win over Arsenal led to clashes with police.
cards.body:
Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory over Arsenal sparked violent clashes across France. More than 280 people were arrested nationwide as celebrations descended into chaos, with over 130 arrests in Paris alone.

Police deployed thousands of officers to manage the crowds of fans, some of whom fired flares during the unrest. Authorities worked to contain the disturbances that erupted following PSG's championship win.

cards.headline: Japan defense minister rejects militarism accusations, criticizes China's weapons buildup
cards.teaser: Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi denied charges of militarism while making pointed remarks about China's arsenal in an escalating dispute over Japan's military expansion.
cards.body:
Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi rejected China's accusations of neo-militarism, delivering some of Tokyo's strongest remarks yet in the dispute over military expansion. He characterized Japan as a "peace-loving" nation while criticizing China for expanding its military capabilities "without sufficient transparency."

cards.headline: Five people rescued from flooded cave in Laos after more than a week
cards.teaser: Rescue teams freed five people trapped in a flooded cave in Laos in a hazardous operation, with some survivors freeing themselves.
cards.body:
Four more miners have been freed from a flooded cave in Laos where they had been trapped for 10 days. The rescue operation involved divers navigating through narrow tunnels filled with muddy water and sharp rocks to reach the trapped men. One person was rescued on Friday, followed by four additional rescues.

Two of the seven villagers who entered the cave on May 20 while searching for gold remain missing. Rescue teams continue their efforts to locate them as they work through the hazardous conditions underground.

cards.headline: Israeli soldiers describe ongoing killings in Gaza despite ceasefire
cards.teaser: Israeli soldiers provided rare firsthand accounts from Gaza, telling reporters that killings continue despite an official ceasefire.

cards.headline: Ecuador accused of interfering in Colombia election with tariff offer
cards.teaser: Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa offered to cancel tariffs after speaking with a Colombian right-wing candidate ahead of the country's vote.
cards.body:
Ecuador faces accusations of interfering in Colombia's presidential election after President Daniel Noboa offered to cancel tariffs following a conversation with a right-wing presidential candidate. The pledge came shortly before Sunday's vote.

The timing of the tariff cancellation announcement raised concerns about foreign interference in the Colombian electoral process. The move linked a significant economic policy decision directly to contact with one candidate during an active campaign.

hero.headline: 11 workers killed in chemical tank collapse at Washington paper mill
hero.body:
Eleven workers died after a chemical tank collapsed at a paper mill in Longview, Washington. Officials have recovered and identified all victims from the incident at the Nippon mill.

The collapse occurred at the Longview facility, where a chemical storage tank imploded. Authorities worked to recover the bodies of the workers who were killed in the accident.

Local officials completed the recovery operation and released the names of all 11 workers who died. The families of the victims have been notified.

The Nippon paper mill is mourning the loss of the workers. The facility experienced what officials described as a tank implosion that led to a chemical spill.

The exact cause of the tank collapse has not been detailed in available reports. The incident represents one of the deadliest workplace accidents in recent Washington state history.

Authorities initially reported nine workers missing after the collapse. The death toll was later confirmed at 11 as recovery efforts concluded.

The chemical tank failure caused an explosion at the paper mill facility. Emergency responders worked to secure the site and recover the victims.

The Longview community is processing the loss of the workers. The paper mill employs a significant number of local residents.

Investigators are expected to examine the circumstances that led to the tank collapse. The incident raises questions about safety procedures at industrial facilities that handle hazardous chemicals.

The Nippon mill manufactures paper products. The facility uses various chemicals in its production processes, which are stored in large tanks on site.

All victims have now been identified and their names released to the public. The recovery operation concluded with all bodies accounted for from the collapse site.

cards.headline: Bus driver charged after crash kills five in Virginia
cards.teaser: A charter bus driver faces involuntary manslaughter charges after a crash on Interstate 95 killed five people, including a family of four traveling to a wedding.
cards.body:
A charter bus driver has been charged with involuntary manslaughter following a crash on Interstate 95 in Virginia that killed five people and injured 34 others. The collision involved the bus hitting multiple cars.

Among the dead were four members of a family who were traveling to a wedding. The crash occurred when the charter bus struck other vehicles on the highway. Transportation Secretary Duffy pointed to the driver's language in commenting on the incident, calling it unacceptable.

cards.headline: Judge blocks Trump's Kennedy Center plans and orders name removal
cards.teaser: A federal judge ruled against President Trump's plans for the Kennedy Center and ordered the removal of his name from the venue.
cards.body:
A federal judge issued a ruling blocking President Trump's plans for the Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. The court also ordered the removal of Trump's name from the cultural institution.

Trump responded to the decision by criticizing the judge's wife. The ruling has created uncertainty for the Kennedy Center as it enters what one publication described as unknown territory. The decision represents a legal setback for the president's vision for the venue.

cards.headline: Trump receives physical exam showing leg swelling and hand bruising
cards.teaser: The White House released results from President Trump's latest physical examination, which found him in excellent health despite some swelling and bruising.
cards.body:
President Trump underwent a physical examination, and his doctor released results describing him as in excellent health. The exam noted leg swelling and bruising on his hands.

The doctor recommended Trump lose weight and exercise more. The White House released the physical exam results publicly. Medical staff assessed the president's overall condition as excellent despite the minor issues noted in the examination.

cards.headline: California primary features close race for governor
cards.teaser: California voters head to the polls for a gubernatorial primary where recent polling shows candidate Becerra ahead of the field.
cards.body:
California's June 2 primary election will narrow the gubernatorial field to two candidates, with Democrats Xavier Becerra and Tom Steyer competing alongside Republican Steve Hilton in a tight three-way race. The election also includes a competitive Los Angeles mayoral contest and congressional races that could influence control of the US House.

Voters heading into Tuesday's primary appear frustrated and underwhelmed, with little clarity emerging in the final campaign stretch. The governor's race to succeed term-limited Democrat Gavin Newsom remains volatile, while Los Angeles voters are divided on whether to reelect embattled Mayor Karen Bass or support a challenger.

cards.headline: Four inmates escape Alabama correctional facility
cards.teaser: Authorities are searching for four inmates who escaped from a correctional center in Alabama.
cards.body:
Four inmates escaped from a correctional facility in Alabama, prompting a search by authorities. Law enforcement is working to locate the escapees.

The inmates fled from the correctional center, though the circumstances of their escape were not detailed in initial reports. A manhunt is underway to recapture the four individuals who left the facility.

cards.headline: Hundreds arrested after Champions League celebrations turn violent in France
cards.teaser: French police arrested hundreds of people after celebrations of PSG's Champions League victory over Arsenal led to unrest.
cards.body:
Hundreds of people were arrested in France as celebrations following Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory over Arsenal descended into disorder. Thousands of police officers were deployed to manage the crowds and control the unrest that erupted.

During the festivities, some fans fired flares as they celebrated PSG's retention of the title. The celebrations escalated into violence, leading law enforcement to conduct mass arrests across the affected areas.

hero.headline: Anthropic Raises $65 Billion, Surpasses OpenAI in Valuation
hero.body:
Anthropic has raised $65 billion in its latest funding round, reaching a post-money valuation of $965 billion and making it more valuable than OpenAI. The Series H funding round marks a significant shift in the artificial intelligence industry's competitive landscape.

The seven cofounders of Anthropic are now worth a combined $116 billion following the fundraising. The company, which develops AI systems including the Claude language model, has attracted substantial investor interest as the AI sector continues to expand.

Analysts view the funding as part of a broader trend in artificial intelligence investment. Dan Ives described Anthropic's growth as just the beginning of a larger AI rally across the technology sector.

The valuation surge comes as major technology companies and investors pour capital into AI development. Anthropic has positioned itself as a key player in the race to build advanced AI systems, competing directly with OpenAI and other well-funded rivals.

The funding round represents one of the largest in recent venture capital history. It reflects investor confidence in Anthropic's technology and business model, as well as expectations for future growth in the AI market.

The company has focused on developing what it describes as safe and beneficial AI systems. Its rapid valuation increase demonstrates the premium investors place on leading AI technology companies in the current market environment.

Anthropic's rise above OpenAI in valuation marks a notable development in the AI industry, where the two companies have been viewed as primary competitors. The funding gives Anthropic substantial resources to continue developing its technology and expanding its operations in a field characterized by high research and development costs.

cards.headline: China Factory Activity Declines Further
cards.teaser: Manufacturing activity in China weakened in the latest reporting period, adding to concerns about the country's economic trajectory.
cards.body:
Factory activity in China deteriorated in recent measurements, providing another warning signal about the state of the world's second-largest economy. The decline in manufacturing performance adds to existing concerns about China's economic health.

The worsening factory data comes as China faces broader economic challenges. Manufacturing activity serves as a key indicator of economic momentum, and its continued weakness suggests ongoing pressure on the country's industrial sector.

cards.headline: Blue Origin Receives National Security Contract Hours Before Rocket Explosion
cards.teaser: The space company secured a military launch task order just before an explosion damaged its New Glenn rocket and launch complex.
cards.body:
Blue Origin received a national security launch task order hours before a New Glenn rocket exploded during a hotfire test at Cape Canaveral in Florida. The massive fireball destroyed the launchpad at the Kennedy Space Center on Thursday night at 9pm ET, with the orange glow visible over 115 miles away in Fort Pierce. No personnel were harmed in the incident.

The explosion was called an "anomaly" by the company. Blue Origin has since regained access to Launch Complex 36. NASA's lunar base plans and goal to return humans to the moon within two years were jeopardized by the setback for Jeff Bezos's company.

cards.headline: SoftBank Plans $75 Billion Investment in French AI Data Centers
cards.teaser: The Japanese conglomerate announced plans to build what would be Europe's largest AI facility in France.
cards.body:
SoftBank announced plans to invest up to €75 billion in French AI data centers, positioning the project as Europe's largest AI infrastructure development. The investment will focus on building and operating up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity to meet growing demand for AI computing infrastructure across the continent.

CEO Masayoshi Son confirmed the investment strategy, highlighting the company's commitment to expanding technological capabilities in Europe as the artificial intelligence sector continues to grow rapidly.

cards.headline: United Airlines Flight Diverted After Passenger Attempts to Breach Cockpit
cards.teaser: A flight bound for Minneapolis was rerouted to Wisconsin after a passenger allegedly tried to access the cockpit multiple times.
cards.body:
United Airlines diverted a flight from Chicago to Minneapolis after a passenger attempted to breach the cockpit. The plane landed in Madison, Wisconsin, where law enforcement responded to the incident.

The 75-year-old passenger was arrested following the emergency diversion. The FBI declined to pursue charges against him.

cards.headline: China's Biotechnology Industry Expands Drug Development Efforts
cards.teaser: Clinical trials conducted in China are drawing attention as the country's pharmaceutical sector grows rapidly.
cards.body:
Clinical trials conducted in China garnered significant attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago. The visibility reflects China's growing involvement in global drug development.

China's biotechnology sector has experienced rapid expansion, intensifying concerns about declining U.S. dominance in the field. The country's advancing capabilities in drug development are reshaping competitive dynamics in the pharmaceutical industry.

cards.headline: Ferrari Faces Criticism Over First Electric Vehicle Design
cards.teaser: The Italian automaker's Luce EV has drawn backlash from some observers who say it departs from the brand's traditional design philosophy.
cards.body:
Ferrari's first electric vehicle, the Luce, has been heavily criticized following its introduction. Some critics said the design represents a departure from Ferrari's roots and traditional styling approach.

The company had positioned the Luce as its response to competition from Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers. The backlash following the unveiling suggests challenges for traditional luxury automakers as they transition to electric powertrains while attempting to maintain brand identity.

hero.headline: Meteor explodes over Massachusetts, causing sonic booms across New England
hero.body:
A meteor exploded over northeastern Massachusetts and southeastern New Hampshire on Saturday afternoon, creating sonic booms that echoed across the region with a blast equivalent to 300 tons of TNT, according to NASA.

The fireball broke up just after 2pm local time at an altitude of 40 miles while traveling at 75,000 miles per hour, NASA's deputy news chief Jennifer Dooren said in a statement to AFP. The explosion was powerful enough to be heard and felt by hundreds of people across parts of New England, with reports coming in from a wide geographic area.

Residents across the Boston metropolitan area were among those who experienced the loud boom firsthand. The sonic boom traveled considerable distances through the atmosphere, allowing people across multiple states to hear and feel the effects of the explosion. The event prompted widespread reports from concerned residents trying to identify the source of the mysterious noise.

When meteoroids enter Earth's atmosphere at extreme speeds, they create sonic booms as they break apart due to atmospheric pressure and friction. In this case, the meteor's rapid descent and fragmentation at high altitude produced enough sound energy to be detected across a broad region.

The explosion occurred at such a high altitude that most of the meteor burned up completely in the atmosphere. Experts noted that while there could be some small fragments, the majority of the material would have been consumed by the intense heat generated during atmospheric entry and breakup. So far, no reports of meteor fragments or damage from falling debris have been associated with this event.

The meteor that caused Saturday's explosion was a space rock entering Earth's atmosphere from above Lake Erie. Its fragmentation over the northeastern United States generated the powerful sonic boom that startled residents across the region.

This event is part of a broader phenomenon. According to one study, approximately 17,000 meteorites fall to Earth annually. Most space rocks smaller than a football field break apart in Earth's atmosphere before reaching the ground. On very rare occasions, they may explode in the air like the meteor that affected Massachusetts and New Hampshire on Saturday.

NASA confirmed the event through data analysis and satellite information, which helped establish the meteor's path, speed, and the location where it fragmented. The agency's meteoroid environment office provided details about the incident to news organizations and the public.

The explosion demonstrates how dramatic and noticeable meteor impacts can be, even when the rocks burn up completely in the upper atmosphere. Residents in the affected region experienced firsthand the power of a space rock entering Earth's atmosphere at extreme velocity.

cards.headline: Microsoft threatens legal action against cybersecurity researchers
cards.teaser: Microsoft has threatened security researchers with criminal investigation after they disclosed software exploits.
cards.body:
Microsoft is facing backlash over its response to security researchers disclosing zero-day exploits. A researcher using the alias Nightmare Eclipse has publicly shared proof-of-concept exploit code and engaged in a public dispute with the company, with some posts suggesting they may be a former employee.

Microsoft's legal threats against the disclosure have drawn criticism from the cybersecurity community, including researcher Kevin Beaumont, who highlighted the company's approach as particularly noteworthy in how it handles vulnerability disclosures.

cards.headline: Windows PCs powered by Nvidia chips to launch next week
cards.teaser: The first Windows computers running on Nvidia processors will debut next week, according to reports.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm are set to introduce the first Windows PCs powered by Nvidia's new N1X laptop processors next week at Computex. This marks Nvidia's entry into the PC processor market.

Nvidia has been building anticipation for the announcement with cryptic social media posts ahead of the event, signaling the significance of the processor launch for the company.

cards.headline: SoftBank to invest up to $75 billion in French data centers
cards.teaser: SoftBank announced plans to invest up to $75 billion to build data center infrastructure in France.
cards.body: SoftBank plans to invest up to €75 billion in constructing data centers across France. The company intends to develop and operate up to 5 gigawatts of additional data center capacity through this expansion.

cards.headline: James Bond video game '007: First Light' becomes major sales success
cards.teaser: The new James Bond game has achieved significant 24-hour sales figures following its release.
cards.body:
'007: First Light' has become a major sales success, with the game recording substantial sales in its first 24 hours. Developed by IO Interactive, the studio behind the Hitman franchise, the game explores Bond's early years before he became a 00 agent.

The game is available on PC, Xbox, and PlayStation 5. Reviews have praised it as a triumphant Bond title, with critics noting that IO Interactive's expertise in stealth gameplay and eye for architectural detail made them well-suited to bring the character to life. The release marks a significant moment for the James Bond franchise in gaming.

cards.headline: AC unveils new Cobra supercar with up to 720 horsepower
cards.teaser: British carmaker AC has released a production model of its Cobra Coupe featuring a supercharged V8 engine.
cards.body:
AC, Britain's oldest active carmaker, has officially debuted its new Cobra Coupe production model. The two-seat sports car features a Ford 5.0-liter V8 engine with up to 720 horsepower in its supercharged configuration, with another variant offering 799 horsepower.

The vehicle is priced between $315,000 and $500,000 depending on configuration. The new Cobra represents a return to form for the iconic British brand, combining modern supercar performance with the classic Cobra design heritage.

cards.headline: Rare full moon to appear as smallest and dimmest of the year
cards.teaser: A blue micromoon will be visible this weekend, marking the second full moon of May and the farthest from Earth this year.
cards.body:
A full moon will appear this weekend as the farthest, smallest, and dimmest of the year, according to NASA. The moon is classified as a blue micromoon because it is the second full moon occurring within the month of May.

The phenomenon represents a rare occurrence in the lunar calendar. The moon's distance from Earth during this phase makes it appear smaller and less bright than typical full moons throughout the year.

hero.headline: Wembanyama leads Spurs past Thunder to NBA Finals
hero.body:
Victor Wembanyama scored 22 points and secured the Western Conference Finals MVP award as the San Antonio Spurs defeated the defending champion Oklahoma City Thunder 111-103 in Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals on Saturday night. The victory advances the Spurs to the NBA Finals, where they will face the New York Knicks in a matchup beginning Wednesday in San Antonio.

Wembanyama's performance proved decisive in the series-clinching game, though his teammates contributed significantly to the upset. Julian Champagnie added 20 points and made six three-pointers, while Dylan Harper provided crucial bench scoring. Luke Kornet, Wembanyama's backup center, also made an impact with a crucial block in the fourth quarter as the Thunder mounted a comeback attempt.

The 22-year-old Wembanyama was emotional following the victory, describing the moment as a realization of a childhood dream. "We're still hungry, we want more. This feeling is so powerful, I can't explain it," he said after the game.

The Thunder played without Jalen Williams due to a hamstring injury and found themselves unable to overcome the Spurs down the stretch. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, the reigning NBA MVP, delivered a strong performance with 35 points and nine assists, but no other Thunder player scored more than 20 points. The defending champions were forced to launch hopeful three-pointers from well outside the arc in the final moments as San Antonio secured a breakaway dunk to seal the win.

Thunder coach Mark Daigneault acknowledged the difficult loss but remained optimistic about his team's future. "You have to grow from every experience, including the tough ones," he said. "There's nobody that we don't think we can beat, respectfully."

The Spurs' Finals appearance marks their first since 2014, when they defeated the Miami Heat for their fifth championship. This upcoming Finals matchup against the Knicks carries historical significance, as the teams previously met in the 1999 NBA Finals with the Spurs winning that series 4-1 for their first championship. The franchises also faced each other earlier this season in the NBA Cup final.

Champagnie expressed confidence in the Spurs' prospects going forward. "We never knew if we were going to get this far but when you've got the greatest player in the world things happen," he said after the game.

The Knicks secured their Finals berth earlier in the playoffs and are seeking their first championship since 1973. The Spurs, meanwhile, are pursuing their sixth title in franchise history. Game 1 of the Finals is set for Wednesday in San Antonio, with ticket prices already updated following the conclusion of the Western Conference Finals.

cards.headline: Hockey player Claude Lemieux dies at 60
cards.teaser: Four-time Stanley Cup champion Claude Lemieux has died at age 60.
cards.body:
Claude Lemieux, a four-time Stanley Cup champion, died at age 60. His family announced they are donating his brain to the Boston University CTE Center for research into chronic traumatic encephalopathy.

Lemieux won Stanley Cup titles during a career that spanned multiple NHL teams. The donation to Boston University will contribute to ongoing research into the long-term effects of head trauma in professional hockey players.

cards.headline: Serrano equals women's boxing knockout record
cards.teaser: Amanda Serrano stopped Cheyenne Hanson in the second round to equal the record for most knockouts in women's boxing history.
cards.body:
Amanda Serrano made history by equaling the record for most knockouts in women's boxing with her dominant performance against Cheyenne Hanson in Texas. The fight ended decisively in the second round, cementing Serrano's place among the sport's all-time greats.

The victory also allowed Serrano to retain her WBA and WBO featherweight titles, further solidifying her position as one of boxing's elite champions.

cards.headline: Hundreds arrested after Paris Champions League celebrations
cards.teaser: Police arrested hundreds of people as crowds celebrated PSG's Champions League victory over Arsenal.
cards.body:
More than 130 people were arrested in Paris after Paris Saint-Germain won the Champions League against Arsenal on Saturday. The club's supporters celebrated throughout the city, with thousands of police officers deployed to manage the crowds at hotspots including the Parc de Princes stadium, where over 40,000 fans watched the match on giant screens.

Tensions escalated as some supporters aimed fireworks at police, who responded with teargas. Footage showed brief skirmishes near the stadium as officers worked to control the unrest following PSG's penalty shootout victory in Budapest.

cards.headline: Transgender athlete wins California state track medals
cards.teaser: Transgender senior AB Hernandez won medals at the California state track and field championships.
cards.body:
AB Hernandez, a transgender senior from Jurupa Valley, won medals at the California state track and field meet. The athlete topped qualifying scores again at the CIF championships, which drew protests.

Police were summoned to the meet after a press conference involving the transgender athlete descended into chaos. Hernandez's mother spoke out as the championships continued amid the protests.

cards.headline: North Carolina defeats East Carolina in NCAA regional
cards.teaser: A three-run homer from Hynek helped North Carolina defeat East Carolina 7-5 in the Chapel Hill Regional.
cards.body:
North Carolina defeated East Carolina 7-5 in the winner's bracket of the Chapel Hill Regional. Hynek hit a three-run homer that sparked the Tar Heels' victory in the NCAA baseball tournament game.

The win advanced North Carolina in the Chapel Hill Regional bracket. NC State was eliminated from the NCAA tournament, ending coach Avent's coaching run.

cards.headline: Steveson dominates in RAF wrestling debut
cards.teaser: Gable Steveson defeated Alexander Romanov by technical fall in his RAF wrestling debut.
cards.body:
Gable Steveson won his RAF wrestling debut, defeating Alexander Romanov by technical fall at RAF 9. Merab Dvalishvili also dominated in his bout on the card.

The event also featured Colby Covington facing Chris Weidman. A matchup between Arman Tsarukyan and Colby Covington was set for July following the RAF 9 results.

hero.headline: Matt Brown, Star of 'Alaskan Bush People,' Dead at 42
hero.body:
Matt Brown, a cast member of the Discovery Channel reality series 'Alaskan Bush People,' has died at 42. His brother Noah helped pull his body from a river.

Authorities had been searching for a missing man believed to be Brown after he was spotted near a river. The search was later suspended. Brown's brother Bear confirmed that Matt had been seen near the river where the body was found.

Brown appeared on 'Alaskan Bush People,' which followed the Brown family living in remote Alaska. The show documented their off-the-grid lifestyle and attempts at self-sufficiency in the wilderness.

The series, which premiered in 2014, featured Matt Brown alongside his parents and siblings. The family became known to viewers through their isolated existence and survival skills in the Alaskan backcountry.

Matt Brown had been part of the show since its beginning, appearing in numerous episodes over the years. His participation in the series made him recognizable to fans of the reality program.

The circumstances surrounding Brown's death involve his presence near a river where search efforts had been concentrated. His brother Noah's involvement in recovering the body underscores the tragic nature of the incident for the Brown family.

Brown's death marks a loss for the 'Alaskan Bush People' cast and the show's audience. The program continued to air through multiple seasons, building a following among viewers interested in wilderness living and family dynamics in extreme environments.

The reality star's passing comes after years in the public eye through the Discovery Channel series. His role on the show contributed to its portrayal of the challenges and experiences of living remotely in Alaska.

cards.headline: Italy Bans Kanye West and Travis Scott Concerts Over Security Concerns
cards.teaser: Italian authorities have canceled scheduled July concerts by Kanye West and Travis Scott at a northern Italy venue.
cards.body:
Italian authorities have cancelled a Kanye West concert scheduled for July 18 at the RCF Arena in Reggio Emilia, citing public order and safety concerns. The city's prefect, Salvatore Angieri, made the decision after the local Jewish community raised concerns about West's previous antisemitic remarks.

West, who changed his name to Ye in 2021, was set to perform at the Pulse of Gaia festival. The cancellation affects the 48-year-old rapper's planned appearance at the venue in northern Italy.

cards.headline: Love Island USA Removes Second Contestant in Two Years Over Use of Racial Slur
cards.teaser: Peacock's reality dating series has dismissed Vasana Montgomery after social media posts showed her using a racial slur.
cards.body:
Love Island USA has removed cast member Vasana Montgomery from Season 8 following the emergence of social media posts containing racial slurs. The dismissal was announced two days after the season's cast reveal, ahead of the show's June 2 premiere on Peacock.

This marks the second consecutive year the dating reality series has removed an islander for using offensive language on social media. The recurring pattern reflects ongoing conduct issues within the show's casting process.

cards.headline: Jay-Z Performs at Roots Picnic in Philadelphia with Jazmine Sullivan and Meek Mill
cards.teaser: The rapper headlined the Philadelphia festival after changing his streaming name back to its original spelling.
cards.body:
Jay-Z headlined the Roots Picnic in Philadelphia, performing alongside Jazmine Sullivan, Bilal, and Meek Mill. The concert followed months of preparation that included the rapper changing his streaming name from Jay-Z to its original spelling, JA-Z.

The performance brought what the artist described as New York flair to the Philadelphia venue. The show represented a return to the earlier spelling of his name across streaming platforms ahead of the festival appearance.

cards.headline: Horror Producers Jason Blum and James Wan Credit Low-Budget Films for Industry Success
cards.teaser: Blum compared the current box office performance of films like 'Backrooms' and 'Obsession' to the filmmaking era of the 1970s.
cards.body:
Jason Blum credited the box office success of horror films 'Backrooms' and 'Obsession' with helping the film industry. The producer compared the current moment to the atmosphere of 1970s cinema, describing a similar feeling in the industry.

Blum and James Wan discussed the rise of YouTube filmmakers and their goal of building what they called a 'Disney of Horror.' Wan stated that horror saves Hollywood, while Blum drew parallels between the low-budget horror boom and edgy movies from the 1970s.

cards.headline: Trump Offers to Perform at Freedom 250 Concert After Artists Withdraw
cards.teaser: The former president suggested he could perform himself at the event, saying only great patriots would be invited.
cards.body:
Donald Trump offered to perform at the Freedom 250 concert himself after several artists withdrew from the series. He stated that only great patriots would be invited to participate in the event.

Performers including Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride declined to participate, citing concerns that the event would become political. Trump responded by proposing a "wild" rally format as an alternative to traditional concerts for the 250th anniversary celebration.

cards.headline: 'Only Murders in the Building' Wins Outstanding Scripted Series at CrimeCon Clue Awards
cards.teaser: Hulu took home two major awards at the 2026 ceremony, including prizes for both scripted and documentary crime content.
cards.body:
Hulu's 'Only Murders in the Building' won the award for outstanding scripted series at the 2026 CrimeCon Clue Awards. The streaming service also received recognition for its docuseries 'Girl on the Run: The Hunt for Americas Most Wanted,' which won outstanding docuseries.

The winners were announced at the ceremony held on a recent Saturday. CBS's '48 Hours' was also among the programs recognized at this year's Clue Awards, which honor crime-related television content.

hero.headline: Zelensky warns of major Russian attacks within 48 hours
hero.teaser: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he expects Russia to launch major attacks within the next two days based on intelligence from the U.S. and European allies.
hero.body:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is preparing for a major Russian attack that he expects to occur within the next 48 hours. The warning is based on intelligence shared by the U.S. and European allies.

Zelensky said he believes the attacks will happen either tonight or tomorrow night. He indicated the anticipated assault would be significant in scale based on the intelligence assessments provided by Western partners.

cards.headline: Trump requests changes to Iran deal negotiated by his envoys
cards.teaser: President Trump has asked for several amendments to the deal his envoys reached with Iranian counterparts, according to a senior administration official and a s.
cards.body:
President Trump asked his advisers to make amendments to a framework agreement reached between U.S. and Iranian negotiators, according to administration officials. The president met with his team to make what he described as his "final determination" on the deal during a Friday Situation Room meeting.

The tentative agreement would extend the current ceasefire and reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Trump's requested changes have initiated another round of negotiations between the parties as both sides work to finalize terms.

cards.headline: Justice Department seeks judge's recusal from Georgia election case
cards.teaser: The Justice Department asked a federal judge to step aside from overseeing its lawsuit against Georgia election officials after she attended an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis.
cards.body:
The Justice Department filed a motion on Friday asking a federal judge to recuse herself from the department's lawsuit against Georgia election officials. The request was submitted to the U.S. District Court.

The department argued that the judge's attendance at an event honoring Fulton County District Attorney Fani Willis raises questions about her ability to remain impartial in the case. The filing contends this appearance creates concerns about whether she can fairly oversee the litigation.

cards.headline: UN adds Israeli and Russian forces to sexual violence blacklist
cards.teaser: The United Nations placed Israeli and Russian security forces on its annual blacklist documenting sexual violence during conflict for the first time.
cards.body:
The United Nations included Israeli and Russian security forces on its annual blacklist for sexual violence during conflict for the first time in a report released Friday. The U.N. document identifies 77 government and non-government parties credibly suspected of patterns of rape or other sexual violence.

The additions follow allegations of rape against detained Palestinians by Israeli forces. The blacklist tracks parties across multiple countries engaged in ongoing conflicts where sexual violence has been documented.

cards.headline: Lead prosecutor steps down from Comey criminal case
cards.teaser: The federal prosecutor who secured an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has stepped away from the case, according to a court filing.
cards.body:
The federal prosecutor who obtained an indictment against former FBI Director James Comey has stepped down from the case. A notice of substitution was filed in the Eastern District of North Carolina on Friday.

Comey was indicted for allegedly threatening the life of President Trump in a social media post featuring seashells that has since been deleted. The prosecutor, Matthew, secured the indictment before stepping away, though the filing did not provide a reason for the change.

cards.headline: Judge to review Trump's $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund
cards.teaser: A judge agreed to review President Trump's $1.8 billion fund, which has sparked a backlash and exposed divisions within the Republican Party.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Miami has reopened Trump's lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service, which seeks $10 billion over the leak of his personal and business tax returns by a former contractor. The reopening came after a third-party motion challenged the settlement's legitimacy, claiming the $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund lacks sufficient detail and may constitute collusion and fraud.

The fund has generated significant controversy since its announcement, creating rifts within the Republican Party. Judge Kathleen Williams's decision to revisit the case means the settlement will face judicial scrutiny regarding its structure and implementation.

cards.headline: New Jersey governor and DHS secretary coordinate on ICE facility protests
cards.teaser: New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin found common ground after state police were deployed to a Newark immigration detention center facing protests.
cards.body:
Protests at the Delaney Hall immigration detention center in Newark, New Jersey continued on Saturday as a hunger and labor strike by detained immigrants reached its ninth day. The detainees are demanding improved conditions and medical care.

State police deployed barricades at the facility as competing demonstrations intensified. Trump supporters gathered to express backing for ICE enforcement, while other protesters advocated for the detained immigrants. The two groups faced off across the police barriers set up to maintain order.
